title: The Yellow Wallpaper
focus: confinement driving a woman into madness

teacherSummary.text: A woman recovering from what her physician husband John calls a 'temporary nervous depression' after childbirth keeps a secret journal during a summer 'rest cure' in an old mansion. Forbidden to write or work, she is confined to a nursery with barred windows and hideous yellow wallpaper. She comes to see a woman trapped behind its pattern. On the last night she tears the paper off to free her, identifies with her, and creeps around the room; John faints at the sight.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “There are things in that paper that nobody knows but me” slowly and put it in my own words: She insists that the wallpaper holds secrets and that she alone can see them. Next, craft. I notice the claim is private and proud, using "nobody... but me," which cuts her off from everyone else. The strongest word is “nobody”: it makes her knowledge feel special but also lonely, the sign of a mind being shut in. Then, effect. What does the narrator mean when she says only she knows the things in the paper? My answer: When she says only she knows the things in the paper, the narrator means her isolation has turned the wallpaper into her private world; what she sees there is really her own trapped situation, which no one around her will acknowledge.

hsFreshman.note: Use the scaffolds for literal and inferential items; require one quotation for every inferential answer.

hsJunior.note: Emphasize structure and ambiguity; students should name where the text leaves matters open.

contentNotes.teacherNote: Sensitive content: Postpartum depression and psychosis; controlling marriage; suicidal thoughts. Preview the story, tell students in advance, and allow a pass on reading aloud. Keep discussion on how the writer uses these elements, not on graphic detail. This section mentions drinking or a drug (“…and lots of tonics and things, to say nothing of ale and wine and rare meat. Dear John! He l…”). Treat it as period custom or plot detail; name it plainly and don't glamorize it.
